T0611.title: Functional Safety
T0611.definition: The engineering discipline of ensuring a system remains in or enters a safe state under fault or anomaly via systematic technical and management measures, preventing physical harm and property damage.
T0611.description: Functional safety is the theoretical basis of robot physical safety, ensuring fail-safe behavior via risk assessment, safety-level design (PLd/SIL2), redundant architecture, and self-diagnostics. Robot functional safety follows standards like ISO 10218 (industrial-robot safety, 2025 revision incorporating ISO/TS 15066 cobot content), ISO 13482 (personal-care robot safety), and IEC 62061 (mechanical electrical safety). Functional safety differs from cybersecurity: functional safety guards against random faults, cybersecurity against malicious attacks, but the two are deeply intertwined in embodied intelligence — attackers can exploit cybersecurity vulnerabilities to bypass functional-safety mechanisms (e.g., remotely disabling e-stop), so they require coordinated design.
T0611.usageExample: An industrial robot's functional-safety design requires triggering a safety stop immediately when a force sensor anomaly is detected, preventing a runaway arm from injuring people.
